layout_dets.text: Hieratic. *Cursive form of *Hieroglyphic used in writing *Egyptian

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the 26th century Bc. Replaced by *Demotic, for ordinary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: purposes, from the 7th century Bc, but retained for religious texts;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hence the name ('priestly').

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hieroglyphic. Writing system developed for *Egyptian and used,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mainly on or in monuments, from around 3000 Bc until the 3rd

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: century AD. Replaced for ordinary purposes by *cursive scripts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (*Hieratic, *Demotic) derived from it.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The signs are basically pictures of objects, people, etc., but function

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variously as representations of words as wholes (*logograms), as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representations of consonants or successions of consonants

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (*phonograms), and as *determinatives added to phonograms to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indicate the semantic class to which the word belongs. These functions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are all found in the earliest texts.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range. 2. (Vowel) = close. In the scheme of Chomsky and Halle, *SPE,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: the feature [+ high] is that of a sound produced by ‘raising the body of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the tongue above the level that it occupies in the neutral position':

layout_dets.text: Hindi-Urdu. *Indo-Aryan, native to a large area centred on the valley

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the upper Ganges, but spoken more widely across the north of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Indian subcontinent. The national language of Pakistan, where called

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Urdu and written in an Arabic script derived through Persian, and one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the national languages of India, where called Hindi and written by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: non-Muslims in *Devanagari. Distinct from other modern Indo-Aryan

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hiragana. One of two syllabic systems used in writing *Japanese.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'hissing'. Used of dental or alveolar sibilants such as [s] in hiss, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: opposed to palato-alveolar or ‘hushing' sibilants, such as [S] in hush.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: historical linguistics. The study of change in individual languages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and in language generally. Distinguished by most schools of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *structural linguistics as a branch of the subject concerned with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *diachronic relations among language systems, separate from and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presupposing the findings of *synchronic or *descriptive linguistics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: historic present. A present tense used, especially with an effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of vividness or immediacy, in an account of past events. E.g. 'I was in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Oxford Street yesterday and suddenly this man turns on me and grabs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hittite. *Indo-European language attested by *cuneiform texts of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the 2nd millennium Bc, mainly from the capital of the Hittite empire

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (modern Boğazköy in north central Turkey). The main language of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Anatolian branch.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hixkaryana. *Cariban language in the state of Amazonas in Brazil.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Famous in the history of *typological classification as the first known

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *OVS language.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hjelmslev, Louis (1899-1965). Danish linguist and one of the major

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exponents of *structural linguistics after *Saussure. His most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Prolegomena to a Theory of Language, trans. F. J. Whitfield (1953).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: important theoretical work, Omkring Sprogteoriens Grundlæggelse ('On the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Foundations of Linguistic Theory'), appeared in 1943: later in English,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hjelmslev's theory carried Saussure's concept of the linguistic sign to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: logical conclusion. The sign itself is represented by a 'sign relation' (or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'sign function') between two 'planes' or levels: one of *expression and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one of *content. By the *commutation test, a difference between units

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at one level must entail a difference at the other. At each level, units

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are characterized by their *syntagmatic and *paradigmatic relations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to other units, and these relations constitute a *form (2), again at each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level, independent of its projection onto distinctions of *substance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hjelmslev called his theory 'glossematics' from 1935 onwards.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hmong-Mien. See Miao-Yao.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'hocus pocus'. Coined by F. W. Householder in 1952 in reference to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linguists who did not ascribe any reality to the units, categories, etc.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that they established, as opposed to ‘God's truth' linguists, who did.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hodiernal. (Tense, form of verb) characteristically used to refer to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: events, etc. that have taken place earlier on the day of speaking. From

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Latin hodiernus ‘of today': cf. hesternal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hokan. Proposed family of languages spoken or formerly spoken in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various parts of western North America, from northern California to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Baja California and Sonora; also in the south of Mexico, in parts of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Oaxaca. Yana was a Hokan language studied by Sapir.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hokkien. See Chinese.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stage.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: holophrase. A sentence or utterance consisting of a single word.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Especially of single-word utterances by children at an early stage in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their development of language: called accordingly the holophrastic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homo-. From the Greek word for 'same': thus'homonyms (cf. -onym)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are identical forms with different meanings, *homonymy is a relation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between such forms, and so on.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homographs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homographs. Forms which differ phonetically but are spelled in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same way: e.g. tear [tiə] and tear [tεə]. Cf. homophones.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homonymic clash. A clash between two homonyms, either of which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: could be used in similar contexts. A classic example is a posited clash

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in parts of south-wes't France between a word gat ‘cat', derived from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Latin cattus, and an identical form *gat 'cock', predicted by regular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processes of sound change from Latin gallus. In fact the second was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: replaced by other forms that changed or extended their meaning:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: faisan, historically pheasant', vicaire 'curate', and others. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explanation, proposed by *Gilliéron, is that these replacements

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: avoided the misunderstandings that the clash would often have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: caused.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homonymy. The relation between words whose forms are the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but whose meanings are different and cannot be connected: e.g.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between pen ‘writing instrument' and pen 'enclosure'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Distinguished from *polysemy in that the meanings cannot be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connected: therefore the words are treated as different lexical units.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Also distinguished from cases of *conversion: e.g. for either of these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homonyms, that of pen (noun) to pen (verb). Also from *syncretism,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is between forms of the same paradigm. Further distinctions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be drawn between homonymy of words as lexical units (e.g. the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two lexical units pen) and e.g. identity of *roots or other *morphemes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Also between forms identical in both sound and spelling (such as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two words pen) and those that are the same in spelling only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (*homographs) or in sound regardless of spelling (*homophones).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For 'constructional homonymy' see grammatical ambiguity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homophones. Forms which are homonyms, at least phonetically.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Often therefore of ones spelled differently: e.g. tier and tear [tiə|.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homorganic. (Consonant) which has the same *place of articulation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as one which precedes or follows. Especially of a phonological unit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that must be so realized: thus a nasal consonant in e.g. Italian is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: always homorganic with one which follows: [n] before [t] or [d] (andare

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ‘to go’), [n] before [k] (cinque ‘five’) or [g], and so on.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: honorific (non). Pronoun, form of verb, etc. used in expressing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: respect for someone, e.g. of higher social status. 1. In the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristic use this is a person referred to. E.g. in a sentence in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Japanese meaning ‘The professor helped him', the form for 'helped'

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: might be marked to show respect for the professor who is referred

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to by its subject: this would be a subject honorific. In a sentence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: meaning ‘He helped the professor', it might be marked in a different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: way to show respect for the professor as referred to, in this case,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by its object: this would be an object honorific. 2. Also, in some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accounts, of *polite forms. Such a form is then distinguished, as an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'hushing'

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addressee-controlled honorific, from subject or object honorifics,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are referent-controlled.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hortative. See exhortative.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: host. Form to which e.g. a *clitic attaches. Thus, if -n't is a clitic in He

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: isn't there, it has the host is.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HPSG = Head-Driven Phrase Structure Grammar.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: human. Semantic feature of nouns, etc. characteristically used in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reference to people. Thus who is distinguished from which as human

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ( + human]) vs. non-human ({− human]); girl belongs to a class of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Humboldt, Wilhelm von (1767-1835). Prussian statesman and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scholar, whose book-length introduction to a study of Kawi (Old

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *Javanese), published posthumously in 1836, was described by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Bloomfield, nearly a century later, as 'the first great book on general

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linguistics'. In this and other work that dates essentially from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1820s, Humboldt stressed both the fundamental unity of language in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: general, and the diversity of the individual languages that were seen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as shaping the intellectual life of different nations and societies. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: implied a programme of inquiry in which Humboldt made important

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contributions on three fronts: as a comparativist, whose work on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Javanese included the first comparative study of the *Austronesian or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Malayo-Polynesian family; as a descriptive linguist, also engaging with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Basque among others: and in respect of the distinctions between types

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (*inflecting, *agglutinating, *incorporating) that inform the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grammars of specific languages.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other 'Neo-Humboldtians'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Two particular ideas have been seized on by admirers and followers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: One is Humboldt's emphasis on language not as an object or product

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Greek ergon) but as an activity (energeia) constantly renewed in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interchanges among speakers. The other, which appears rather rarely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in his own work, is that of the inner form' of a specific language,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpreted as the formative principle or principles behind its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: individual grammar and lexicon. This is influential in the 20th

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: century especially in Germany through the work of L. Weisgerber and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the 16th century.
